##  · K5-q-bench — Named-workload latency bench: stand-ins, RTC IRQ source, QEMU icount

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Approved stand-ins at INIT.md manifest weights (steward and driver), both lease paths reported; the goldfish RTC alarm through the real IRQ-handle path; -icount shift=auto per case for sched-* (labelled as instruction time, plus one TCG reference run). Because stand-ins narrow the WP-K5 acceptance, the K5 docs commit adds a rerun-with-real-steward-and-drivers line to WP-S2 and WP-R3 acceptance. Flag to the owner at plan approval.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `1f40c67e6f82c5bbeab7f36bedd48981` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> WP-K5 asks for real-boot acceptance under the named workload: N spinning user budgets at the manifest user weight, one driver and the steward at their manifest weights. It reports the driver's interrupt-to-run latency and the steward's lease-termination latency. Neither the steward (S2) nor native drivers via init (R3) boot yet. Three points:
> 
> (1) Stand-ins. Test programs at the INIT manifest weights (users 100; driver and steward 1000, carved as INIT carves them), launched by a trusted first program. The steward stand-in destroys a lease budget when a timer T fires and measures T to budget_destroy's return; the kernel-deadline lease path is reported too. Is this acceptable for K5's acceptance, with the real steward/driver rerun left to S2/R3?
> 
> (2) The driver's IRQ source is the QEMU virt goldfish RTC alarm: program the alarm at T, then receive on the IRQ handle. Latency is measured on the RTC's own clock, so it's exact and self-contained. OK?
> 
> (3) TCG timing follows host load, so latency and share numbers are noisy and cases may flake. I propose a per-case testbench option to run QEMU with -icount shift=auto for the sched-* cases. That is a small change in tools/testbench, outside K5's kernel paths.
> 
> The numeric target is proposed afterwards in K5-plan with the measured table (p50/p99/max for N = 1, 4, 16, weights, runnable budgets, prior passes), and a package reviewer accepts it.
> 
> Ask: approve (1)-(3), or say what changes.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `baf7cc02ef8949fc1fc7914bedd0cfd0` · 2026-09-24T17:55:33Z

> Approved (1)-(3), with conditions:
> (1) Stand-ins are fine for K5's acceptance, since neither the steward nor native drivers via init exist. Cite the weights from INIT.md's manifest (not only the numbers), and carve the way init will carve. Report both lease paths (the stand-in steward's budget_destroy, and the kernel deadline). This narrows a BUILD-PLAN acceptance line, so in the K5 docs commit add to WP-S2 and WP-R3 acceptance: 'rerun the WP-K5 named-workload latency bench with the real steward and drivers; the numbers must stay within the accepted target.' I'll flag it to the owner at plan approval.
> (2) The goldfish RTC alarm as the IRQ source: OK, if the driver stand-in receives through the kernel's real IRQ-handle path (the device handle and IRQ receive), not a shortcut. State the two clocks: the RTC for alarm-to-run, and rdtime/time_now for the rest. Say whether any conversion is involved.
> (3) -icount shift=auto for sched-* cases: OK as a per-case testbench option. It's a tools/testbench change, reviewed with K5. Two notes: under icount, latency is instruction time, not wall time, so label the table as such, and record one non-icount TCG run as a reference with its noise. Choose sleep=on or off deliberately and say why (idle gaps matter for the idle-floor case).
> The numeric-target flow is as you say: the measured table (p50/p99/max for N = 1, 4, 16, with weights, runnable budgets and prior passes) in K5-plan, and a package reviewer accepts it.
